newsitem.title: UK: Nationwide stops new savers opening accounts.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide stops new savers opening accounts.

text.p: Nationwide, Britain's largest mutually owned building society, said on Wednesday that it will temporarily stop opening accounts for new customers following a recent rush of account openings by so called "carpet-baggers".

The move, which is effective immediately, comes after a stampede by investors to open accounts, hoping that the Nationwide will follow the same route as a recent stream of building societies that have converted to Plc status, giving free shares to members in the process.

"Nationwide has decided to take this step following extremely high levels of account openings as a result of its successful savings initiatives and growing speculative activity," said Nationwide in a statement.
Existing Nationwide customers will not be affected.

The Nationwide is committed to maintaining its mutual status despite the rush of other building societies like Halifax Plc to lose their mutual status. Halifax was floated on the London stock market earlier this month.
